scope: Theorem 5.4 (The global shape lift) of the manuscript “Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar” (preprints/Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Continuous-Caustic-Collar-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 147 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0fefc18481d52acb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Unless the boundary is a circle, there is a single-valued holomorphic function s on the joint tube T =   (y, t) : t is in the parameter disk, −hX(t̄) < ℑy < hX(t) (5.15) such that X(y, t) = Γ(s(y, t)), |ℑs(y, t)| < H. (5.16) It satisfies s(y, 0) = y, s(y + 2π, t) = s(y, t) + 2π, s(y, −t) = s(y, t). (5.17) It also obeys real symmetry, s(ȳ, t̄) = s(y, t). After shrinking the parameter disk, for every real t the real map y 7→ s(y, t) descends to an orientation-preserving analytic circle diffeomorphism. The inequality in (5.16) is void when H = ∞.
